title: Usage drift change-point orchestrator with tenant-aware suppression
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: We have high false positive noise from current usage/cost/latency alerts for multi-tenant customers. Several customers get repeated alerts during known operational windows (billing jobs, scheduled batch traffic), and the on-call burden is increasing. Goal: Build a change-point orchestrator that detects sustained distributional shifts in tenant-level metrics, correlates changes across cost/usage/latency dimensions, and applies tenant-aware suppression and deduplication so that only actionable incidents surface to on-call and product owners.
background: Current pipeline emits per-tenant aggregates every minute into the metrics warehouse. Existing rule-based detectors run thresholds and percentile checks and send alerts to PagerDuty/Slack. Recent incident review (inc-2026-02-billing-spike) flagged >40% of alerts as noise during scheduled backend jobs. We need an automated detector that understands persistent drift vs transient spikes, reduces noise, and provides explainability for each alert (primary metric, magnitude, correlated signals, and suggested remediation).
design_decisions:
- Detection algorithm: prioritize a streaming change-point approach (Bayesian Online Change Point Detection) for low-latency tenant detection plus a daily batch re-evaluation using a robust non-parametric test (E-Divisive or ADWIN) for longer-term regressions.
- Correlation: correlate change-points across metrics (usage, cost, p95 latency) within a 10-minute window and surface combined incidents when >=2 metrics change for the same tenant.
- Suppression: allow policy-based suppression (schedule windows, exempted customers) and adaptive suppression that learns frequent scheduled patterns per-tenant.
- Deduplication: group alerts by tenant + root-cause signature; apply a suppression cooldown (default 6h) after an acknowledged alert.
- Explainability: include a short payload with change magnitude, normalized delta, top correlated routes/endpoints, and a sparkline of the last 6 hours in the alert message.
- Performance: detection must run within existing streaming worker budget (<=200ms additional per-tick) and scale horizontally across partitioned tenant shards.
acceptance_criteria:
1) New orchestrator ingests the same per-minute tenant aggregates and emits a change event stream to the alerting topic.
2) False positive rate for scheduled bulk jobs drops by >=60% in A/B test compared to baseline over 2 weeks.
3) Alert payload includes: primary metric, delta percent, correlated metrics list, recommended next steps, and a link to the tenant detail dashboard.
4) A suppression policy UI hook is plumbed into Console (API only for initial rollout) to mark scheduled windows for tenants.
5) End-to-end latency from metric write to alert event < 2 minutes for streaming-detected incidents.
6) Automated tests + integration test against synthetic drift scenarios are added to CI.
implementation_tasks:
- PR: streaming worker library change (partitioned detectors)
- PR: change-point service (stateless pods) + helm chart updates
- PR: alerting bridge to create structured alert with explainability fields
- DB: add per-tenant schedule table and adaptive suppression model store (key-value)
- Telemetry: dashboard panels and synthetic test harness
- Docs: runbook and run-through for on-call; API docs for suppression policy endpoints
rollout_plan:
1) Canary: enable for 5 low-traffic tenants for 72h (monitor false positives and missed incidents).
2) Expand to 50 tenants with mixed profiles for 7 days while running in parallel with existing detectors (shadow mode).
3) Swap to primary detection for the broader tenant set once FPR target met.
4) Add suppression UI and customer toggle; default suppression off until customer opts in.
5) Post-rollout 14-day observation and revert plan in case of regressions.
risk_and_mitigation:
- Risk: missed true incidents during aggressive suppression. Mitigation: conservative default suppression; require >=2-metric correlation to suppress if magnitude high.
- Risk: compute cost. Mitigation: use tiered detectors (cheap heuristic first, expensive model only on candidates) and shard work by tenant partitions.
- Risk: explainability data volume in alerts. Mitigation: include summary + link to the dashboard instead of full time-series payload.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Ava Chen: Kickoff meeting notes attached in Confluence; scoped streaming + batch components. Decided to prototype BOCPD for low-latency detections.

2026-03-05 - Liam Patel: Initial prototype running on staging, detecting synthetic step-changes. Observed a 45% reduction in noise for our test dataset (scheduled-job cases). Need to tighten grouping logic for deduplication.

2026-03-07 - Maya Singh (SRE): Raised concern about worker memory growth when keeping long-lived posteriors per-tenant. Action: cap posterior history to 1 hour and rely on batch re-eval for long-term patterns.
